title: Kumamoto 2026: the full first seventy-two hours through eleven decision moments
disclosure: This demonstration campaign extends the frozen five-slot reconstruction across the first seventy-two hours. The historical timeline and public observations remain source-bounded. Agent choices are simulated counterfactuals, use the same three graph methods and frozen model sampling settings, and support descriptive comparison only. They are not registered claims and do not show that a simulated choice was better, that responders were wrong, or that lives would have been saved.

observations.plain_text: An internal automatic trigger carried at least a severe regional shaking signal. The exact internal payload is not public.
observations.caveat: This is the minimum reconstructed input consistent with the same-minute mobilization, not an observed archived payload.

observations.plain_text: JMA reported a provisional magnitude of 7.1.
observations.caveat: Provisional at this cutoff.

observations.plain_text: JMA reported a provisional depth of 10 kilometres.
observations.caveat: Revised to 16 kilometres at 20:30:23; that later value is forbidden before then.

observations.plain_text: Uki City reported JMA intensity 7.
observations.caveat: Municipality-level bulletin.

observations.plain_text: Hikawa Town reported JMA intensity 7.
observations.caveat: Municipality-level bulletin.

observations.plain_text: Yatsushiro City reported JMA intensity 6-upper.
observations.caveat: Municipality-level bulletin.

observations.plain_text: Uto City reported JMA intensity 6-upper.
observations.caveat: Municipality-level bulletin.

observations.plain_text: Misato Town reported JMA intensity 6-upper.
observations.caveat: Municipality-level bulletin.

observations.plain_text: Mashiki Town reported JMA intensity 6-upper.
observations.caveat: Municipality-level bulletin.

observations.plain_text: JMA listed Kashima Town as expected at intensity 5-lower or above, but no value was received.
observations.caveat: Missing is not zero and must not be ranked as low intensity.

observations.plain_text: JMA listed Kōsa Town as expected at intensity 5-lower or above, but no value was received.
observations.caveat: Missing is not zero and must not be ranked as low intensity.

observations.plain_text: The 16:35 reissue again reported no received intensity for Kashima Town and Kōsa Town.
observations.caveat: This confirms persistence of the telemetry gap, not the towns' true intensities.

observations.plain_text: Five expressway routes were closed across 21 sections, including the Kyushu and South Kyushu corridors.
observations.caveat: The report does not provide an exact decision time for every closure.

observations.plain_text: The whole Kyushu Shinkansen and 17 conventional lines were suspended; the same report said no railway facility damage was confirmed at that time.
observations.caveat: Suspension is not confirmed rail damage.

observations.plain_text: Water-system problems were reported in Hikawa, Nishihara, Mifune, Ashikita and Minamata.
observations.caveat: The report did not yet list a Yatsushiro water outage.

observations.plain_text: The ministry reported possible deformation behind a quay at Yatsushiro Port.
observations.caveat: Possible, not confirmed damage.

observations.plain_text: The ministry had established hotlines with 36 municipalities across the affected prefectures.
observations.caveat: A hotline is a contact path, not proof that a local damage report had arrived.

observations.plain_text: The MLIT Harukaze helicopter survey was in progress from 18:00 to 18:40.
observations.caveat: No survey result was yet published at 18:10.

observations.plain_text: A collapse was reported at Aeon Mall Kumamoto in Kashima Town, described in the meeting as the site believed to have the heaviest damage.
observations.caveat: A contemporaneous incident report, not a complete casualty count.

observations.plain_text: A factory chimney collapse was reported in Yatsushiro City.
observations.caveat: A contemporaneous incident report, not a complete casualty count.

observations.plain_text: About 47,000 Kumamoto households were without electricity at 20:00.
observations.caveat: Approximate meeting figure.

observations.plain_text: 149 Emergency Fire Response Team units and 535 personnel from Fukuoka, Saga, Ōita and Miyazaki were inbound.
observations.caveat: The minutes do not give exact unit counts per destination.

observations.plain_text: The Ground Self-Defense Force 8th Division was moving toward Aeon Mall Kumamoto with arrival expected around 21:00.
observations.caveat: The minutes do not give an exact personnel count for this movement.

observations.plain_text: No complete national casualty count was publicly available for this allocation decision.
observations.caveat: Do not substitute later municipal death totals.

observations.plain_text: Water-support requests had been received from Yatsushiro City and Kōsa Town, among others.
observations.caveat: A missing request from another municipality is not proof of missing need.

observations.plain_text: Five ministry water trucks and eighteen Japan Water Works Association trucks had already been arranged against requests.
observations.caveat: These 23 are already committed and are not part of the additional 22-truck decision pool.

observations.plain_text: The 12:00 sheet reported about 84,000 households affected at maximum across five prefectures. Named current counts included Kumamoto about 20,000, Yatsushiro about 18,000, Uki about 14,000, Hikawa about 10,500, Uto about 10,000, Kamiamakusa about 8,220, Ashikita about 1,000 and Kōsa about 500.
observations.caveat: Approximate and provisional.

observations.plain_text: JMA later revised the depth from 10 to 16 kilometres.
observations.caveat: Forbidden before 20:30:23.

observations.plain_text: The later liaison table added two officers for Yatsushiro City.
observations.caveat: Forbidden at the 18:10 slot.

observations.plain_text: The water-outage picture later rose to about 108,100 households.
observations.caveat: Forbidden at the 2026-07-29 12:00 slot.

observations.plain_text: The later report counted 20 deaths in Yatsushiro, 7 in Kashima, 5 in Hikawa, 3 in Uki and 1 in Kōsa, plus two not assigned to a named municipality in that breakdown.
observations.caveat: Forbidden as scoring truth for every earlier decision. Deaths are not reported by cause or time.

observations.plain_text: The National Police Agency helicopter television feed from Kumamoto had begun and was available to national decision-makers.
The Governor requested Ground Self-Defense Force disaster dispatch for information gathering, life-saving, supply transport and living support.
Misato Town hall was on emergency power, staff could not enter and the situation could not be confirmed.
Kōsa Town's network was down in the national municipal-function check.
No published casualty count was available when the national and fire headquarters escalated.
A 19:03 aftershock reached JMA intensity 5-lower at Uki City.
Yatsushiro's dispatch command system was recorded restored at 20:00; the public record does not give the failure start time.
observations.caveat: Treating the earthquake minute as the failure start would be an inference.

observations.plain_text: JMA revised the main-shock depth from 10 to 16 kilometres.
The prefecture-wide aggregate reached 506 open shelters holding 9,186 people; it does not reveal individual shelter occupancy.
Three rescue incidents remained active: the Yatsushiro mill chimney, the Kashima shopping centre and two buckled houses in Hikawa.
Eight people had been rescued at the Kashima shopping centre and four of eleven at the Yatsushiro paper mill; work continued in Hikawa and Yatsushiro.
The prefecture-wide aggregate fell to 419 open shelters holding 7,547 people; it does not reveal individual shelter occupancy.
Kagoshima and Okayama battalions were working Yatsushiro, while Fukuoka and Saga battalions were working Kashima.
Memaru district in Yamato Town was recorded isolated by slope failure: four households and six people, reachable on foot with utilities working.
Ground and Maritime Self-Defense Force and Coast Guard water support covered eight named municipalities: Uki, Yatsushiro, Hikawa, Kashima, Uto, Nishihara, Mifune and Kamiamakusa.
An aftershock reached JMA intensity 5-lower at Uki, Kamiamakusa and Amakusa while rescue, shelter and water operations continued.
The prefecture-wide aggregate rose to its recorded occupant peak of 9,931 people across 419 shelters.
The reported water-outage picture had risen to about 108,100 households.
Emergency Fire Response Teams reported 22 people rescued and three rescues still running.
The Ground Self-Defense Force stated that after life-saving operations ended, its centre of gravity would move to water supply and similar support.
The Self-Defense Forces later ran another thorough Kashima search against the seventy-two-hour mark while water support reached 41 sites with 49 vehicles.

unknowns.plain_text: The exact automatic information visible to the FDMA Commissioner at 16:27 is not public.
The readiness and travel time of every unit later mobilized are not published for the 16:27 cutoff.
Kashima and Kōsa had no received municipality value in the real-time main-shock bulletins.
No reviewed public record identifies an action taken specifically because the intensity values were missing.
The public record does not say which non-intensity signals the 18:10 liaison decider considered.
No complete casualty count was available for the 20:00 allocation.
The minutes do not give exact unit or personnel counts for each first-night destination.
Later deaths are not broken down by cause or time, so people alive at a decision cutoff are unknown.
A municipality that had not requested water could still have urgent need.
The 12:00 record does not publish the final municipal split of the additional approximately 22 trucks.
The public record does not state the exact evidence or activity scope behind the 21:00 Maritime Self-Defense Force request.
The two defense dispatch requests do not publish a complete geographic priority or personnel split.
The complete private input to the 18:20 national tier decision is not public.
The public record does not show which observations moving fire units had reported by 18:20.
Official first-night reporting does not provide trustworthy occupancy by municipality or individual shelter.
Shelter feed timestamps mix nominal, opening and publication meanings and cannot score municipal timing.
The Yatsushiro dispatch system failure start time and degraded operating details are not public.
The public record does not provide immediate post-aftershock condition checks for every active site.
The public record does not establish that all response personnel were interchangeable between rescue and water missions.
The public record does not publish a complete personnel split for the final search and water-support expansion.

decision_slots.title: Choose the first outside fire package before a public bulletin exists
decision_slots.decider: Commissioner, Fire and Disaster Management Agency
decision_slots.task: Select up to eight units for immediate movement into the Kumamoto incident area. State which unknowns prevent a precise optimization. Do not use later bulletin, casualty, or mobilization results.

historical_choice.summary: The real 16:27 request named one integrated command unit, three command units, three prefectural battalions and one air unit.
unknowns: The report does not identify Article 44 paragraph 1 or 2.
The exact internal trigger payload and alternative-unit readiness are not public.

assumptions: The exercise candidate pool is limited to real units documented as mobilized by 21:45.
Eligibility of units mobilized later is modeled; their 16:27 readiness is unknown.
Resource mobilization times and notes are hidden from the agent input.
decision_slots.scoring_boundary: Score source/time discipline, constraint validity and explicit unknown handling. Historical package agreement is descriptive only; no outcome advantage is claimed.

decision_slots.title: Decide what to verify when two high-risk towns have no received intensity
decision_slots.task: Assign two modeled verification-priority slots. Missing intensity must be treated as unknown, not zero. The action is a simulated triage test because the public record names no real verification-team resource.

historical_choice.summary: No reviewed public record identifies an action taken specifically because of the missing values; the blank persisted into the 16:35 reissue.
unknowns: The true intensity values were not in the real-time main-shock bulletins.

assumptions: Two verification-priority slots are modeled decision capacity, not claimed real teams.
decision_slots.scoring_boundary: Score whether both persistent missing signals remain live and whether the action cites the two JMA records. Do not score against later deaths.

decision_slots.title: Decide whether the first-night defense request needs a maritime second channel
decision_slots.task: Select one or both defense request channels for the first night. Use only information available by 21:00 and acknowledge that the public record does not disclose the maritime trigger, exact geographic priorities or personnel split.

historical_choice.summary: The Governor made a Ground Self-Defense Force request at 17:30 and a separate Maritime Self-Defense Force Sasebo request at 21:00.
unknowns: The exact trigger and activity scope of the maritime request are not published.

assumptions: Each real request channel is represented as one indivisible resource; this does not model unit or personnel counts.
decision_slots.scoring_boundary: Score source and cutoff discipline, legal channel selection and explicit unknown handling. Historical overlap is descriptive only.

decision_slots.title: Place the first two municipal liaison pairs using the complete 18:10 picture
decision_slots.task: Assign exactly two liaison pairs to two municipalities. Consider intensity, missing telemetry and MLIT's own infrastructure signals without claiming that suspended rail service was confirmed damage.

historical_choice.summary: The real first municipal liaison allocation sent two officers to Uki and two to Hikawa. Yatsushiro was added later.
unknowns: The record does not say which non-intensity signals the liaison decider considered.

assumptions: Each observed two-officer municipal allocation is represented as one indivisible liaison-pair resource.
decision_slots.scoring_boundary: Score time-valid evidence use and legal resource assignments. A different target pair is a divergence, not proof of improvement.

decision_slots.title: Choose the national and fire escalation posture before casualty counts exist
decision_slots.decider: Prime Minister and Commissioner, Fire and Disaster Management Agency
decision_slots.task: Choose exactly one national headquarters posture and one fire mobilization posture. Use the infrastructure, aerial and municipal-function signals available at 18:20; do not use later casualties or incident-site rescue results.

historical_choice.summary: The Prime Minister established the Article 24 Extreme Disaster Management Headquarters and the Fire and Disaster Management Agency switched mobilization from request to instruction.
unknowns: The full private evidence set and moving-unit reports are not public.

assumptions: The four posture options are modeled decision tokens for real legal choices, not deployable units.
decision_slots.scoring_boundary: Score one choice from each posture family, time-valid evidence and unknown handling. A different legal tier is a counterfactual, not an outcome claim.

decision_slots.title: Split the known first-night response between two reported collapse sites
decision_slots.decider: Kumamoto Prefecture disaster headquarters with Emergency Fire Response Team command support
decision_slots.task: Assign the four inbound prefectural battalions and the 8th Division response group across the two reported collapse sites. Use incident reports and resource facts, not later deaths or later rescue totals.

historical_choice.summary: The minutes directed the inbound fleet toward Aeon Mall, explicitly sent the Ōita and Miyazaki battalions to Yatsushiro, and recorded the 8th Division moving to Aeon. They do not publish an exact unit or personnel split by destination.
unknowns: The exact destination of each remaining unit and the personnel split are not stated.
No complete casualty count was available.

assumptions: Each prefectural battalion and the 8th Division response group is one allocation unit; internal unit counts are not invented.
decision_slots.scoring_boundary: Score coverage of both confirmed incident sites, resource validity, evidence traceability and explicit unknowns. Never score by later deaths or claim lives saved.

decision_slots.title: Respond to the first-night shelter load using prefecture aggregates only
decision_slots.task: Choose exactly two prefecture-wide shelter coordination actions after the aggregate moved from 506 shelters and 9,186 occupants to 419 shelters and 7,547 occupants. Do not allocate people, capacity or opening times to a municipality or individual shelter.

historical_choice.summary: The public record preserves only the prefecture aggregate and a first-night instruction linking shelter or wider evacuation to delayed water; it does not expose a matched two-action municipal choice.
unknowns: Municipal and individual shelter occupancy and trustworthy opening clocks are not published.

assumptions: The three eligible actions are modeled coordination choices; the observed aggregate is not spatially distributed.
decision_slots.scoring_boundary: Score aggregate-only discipline, action constraints and explicit unknowns. There is no historical municipal answer key and no outcome score.

decision_slots.title: Allocate first-night rescue support as Yatsushiro dispatch returns
decision_slots.decider: Yatsushiro fire headquarters with Emergency Fire Response Team command support
decision_slots.task: Assign one or two eligible prefectural battalions to the Yatsushiro paper-mill collapse while acknowledging that the dispatch system's failure start, exact degraded procedure, casualty count and unit readiness are unknown.

historical_choice.summary: The Yatsushiro fire headquarters worked the mill collapse with the Miyazaki battalion overnight; Kagoshima and Okayama appear there in the following day's 14:00 record.
unknowns: The failure start, degraded dispatch procedure and exact personnel split are not public.

assumptions: Each battalion is one indivisible allocation unit; the task does not invent an internal personnel count.
decision_slots.scoring_boundary: Score source/time discipline, eligible battalions, the one-site action contract and unknown handling. Later assignments and deaths do not score this choice.

decision_slots.title: Plan additional water support without waiting for every municipality to request it
decision_slots.decider: Japan Water Works Association coordinating with MLIT and the Self-Defense Forces
decision_slots.task: Allocate up to 22 additional water trucks across the named municipalities. Existing requests are evidence, not the only eligibility rule. Quantities must sum to no more than 22 and the already committed 23 trucks cannot be counted again.

historical_choice.summary: The real record says the association coordinated about 22 additional trucks for broad push support without waiting for requests. It does not publish their final municipal split in this sheet.
unknowns: The final municipal split of the additional trucks is not published.
Missing requests do not prove missing need.

assumptions: The report's approximately 22 trucks are represented as a divisible 22-unit pool.
The agent must plan municipal priorities even though the historical 12:00 sheet does not reveal the final split.
decision_slots.scoring_boundary: Score no-wait need reasoning, exact 22-truck constraint, no double counting and source/time integrity. Historical agreement is only push-versus-wait strategy, not a city-by-city answer key.

decision_slots.title: Protect active rescues while turning the regional posture toward water
decision_slots.decider: Ground Self-Defense Force 8th Division with Kumamoto Prefecture
decision_slots.task: Assign three modeled mission priorities across the active rescue sites and regional water mission. Preserve active life-saving work, choose where to place the water-support priority, and reserve attention for the approaching seventy-two-hour search boundary without inventing a personnel split.

historical_choice.summary: The recorded posture kept active rescues running, stated a conditional shift toward water after life-saving ended, and later ran another thorough Kashima search against the seventy-two-hour mark.
unknowns: The complete personnel split and interchangeability between missions are not public.

assumptions: Three modeled priority tokens represent bounded commitments, not personnel or vehicles.
decision_slots.scoring_boundary: Score preservation of active rescue, regional water reasoning, eligible targets and unknown handling. Later mission totals are descriptive context only.

decision_slots.title: Reprioritize two safety checks after the second-night aftershock
decision_slots.task: Assign exactly two immediate safety-verification priorities after the 22:19 intensity-5-lower aftershock. Use the active rescue, isolated-community, shelter and water picture without assuming an unreported site condition.

historical_choice.summary: The public record reports the aftershock and continuing operations but does not name a matched two-target reprioritization decision.
unknowns: Immediate post-aftershock condition checks by active site are not published.

assumptions: Two verification-priority tokens are modeled attention capacity, not real teams.
decision_slots.scoring_boundary: Score use of the aftershock and current operations evidence, valid targets and explicit uncertainty. There is no historical target answer key or outcome claim.

graph_methods.label: Normal summary graph
graph_methods.handoff: Three readers send ordinary prose summaries to the coordinator. Source and time identifiers may be mentioned but no compiler preserves them.

graph_methods.label: Growth-intelligence evidence graph
graph_methods.handoff: Three readers emit claim atoms bound to exact observation identifiers. Deterministic code preserves missing values, source identity and cutoff time in one table before the coordinator decides.
graph_methods.feedback_policy: Mechanical verification records violations but does not revise the model answer.

graph_methods.label: Evidence graph with one constrained feedback loop
graph_methods.handoff: The same evidence table is used. If and only if the deterministic checker finds a source, cutoff, unknown, target or resource violation, it returns that bounded violation list for one revision.
graph_methods.feedback_policy: At most one conditional revision call; no new evidence and no changing the task or resource limits.

limitations: The public record cannot reconstruct every message a real decider saw; each slot lists the exact bounded information set used.
Slot 1 includes a minimum reconstructed automatic trigger and an assumed candidate pool because the exact internal payload and unit readiness are not public.
Slot 2 uses modeled attention capacity because no real verification-team resource is named in the public record.
Historical-choice agreement is descriptive, never the primary score and never proof that one decision was better.
Later deaths, rescues, damage totals, corrected depth, liaison additions and the later water-outage peak are forbidden before their publication times.
No result may say that a simulated allocation saved lives or that real responders were wrong.
This is a demonstration campaign outside the registered five-slot experiment. Its metrics are descriptive and cannot create or repair a registered claim.
Shelter events remain prefecture aggregates; municipal or individual shelter occupancy is never inferred.
Road closure minutes come from a later snapshot and the access-secured record has day precision only; no route-level reopening time is invented.
Modeled decision-capacity resources are labeled in every slot and do not represent real teams, personnel or vehicles.
